arms.better: The run identified the right files, but repeatedly explored after its first useful discovery and ended without attempting the small slice-copy fix. The user-facing failure said the focused continuation repeated exploration and suggested resuming, while reporting that no work was submitted; a recovery mode that immediately acts on the established append-side-effect diagnosis (or gives a direct targeted next step) would have avoided three failed dispatches and made the outcome more useful. The reported telemetry was inconsistent: tm run took about 95 seconds wall-clock while tm stats reported 46 seconds and zero input/output tokens despite 429,435 total tokens, making the effort and cost difficult to interpret.

OpenCode quickly traced the append side effect, copied the arguments before adding the sentinel, wrote a regression test, ran gofmt and go test ./..., and accurately reported the passing result. It first attempted semantic workspace search where no index existed, then recovered with exact searches. A more efficient first route to exact source search and a test aligned exactly with the reported os.Args behavior (the submitted regression test used a direct Execute setup) would improve the run further.
